explanation: About two-thirds of all fresh water is frozen, most of it in Antarctica and Greenland. Nearly all the rest lies underground; lakes and rivers hold a tiny share.

claims.text: About two-thirds (roughly 69%) of Earth's fresh water is held in ice caps and glaciers.
Groundwater holds about 30% of Earth's fresh water, and lakes, rivers and the atmosphere hold far less than the ice does.
Most of the world's ice is in the Antarctic and Greenland ice sheets.
Lakes and rivers hold only a tiny share of Earth's fresh water.
